name: splitter
title: Splitter
summary: Panels side by side with a handle between them that resizes them.
description: Panels side by side (or stacked) with a handle between each pair that resizes them: dragged by the pointer 1:1, stepped by the arrow keys. The handle at rest is the separator's 1px rule in the line colour, so a splitter reads like any divided surface; it darkens under a mouse and turns accent while dragged. An optional grip sits on the rule. Behaviour by Ark UI's splitter (Zag). Sizes are percentages; controlled or uncontrolled.

anatomy.description: Ark's splitter root: a flex row (a column when vertical) as large as its container (the engine sets width and height to 100% and clips). Give it, or its parent, a height. No frame of its own: the caller frames it (a card, a window).

One region, sized by the engine (flex-grow from a zero basis, from its percentage), so it never pads itself. Scrolls its own content when it overflows (the engine's inline overflow: hidden is overridden) and hands the wheel on to the page at its ends.
A panel's content when it is plain text: padded 12px, text.sm ink-2, wrapping anywhere; author text keeps its own direction.

Ark's resize trigger between two panels: role=separator, focusable, the 1px rule in color.line (1px wide in a row, 1px high in a column). Its hit area reaches 4px each side under a mouse (9px) and 20px each side on a coarse pointer (41px), without changing its look. Hovered by a mouse: ink-3; dragged: accent. The cursor is the engine's col-resize / row-resize; touch-action none, so a drag never scrolls the page.

The optional grip (grip prop), Ark's resize trigger indicator: a 12×24 tab centred on the rule by flex centring (never a fractional translate) (24×12 in a column), surface with shadow.btn and radius.chip, holding the dots-six-vertical glyph at 10px in ink-3 (turned a quarter in a column). Decoration; the handle is what is dragged and focused.

panels.description: The panels in order, with their limits. Every pair gets a handle.

size.description: One percentage per panel, adding up to 100. Controlled: size with onSizeChange. Uncontrolled: defaultSize. Without either, the panels share the room equally.

orientation.description: horizontal: panels side by side, the handles are vertical rules. vertical: panels stacked, the handles are horizontal rules.

grip.description: Show the grip on every handle.

keyboardStep.description: Percent an arrow key moves a handle; Shift + arrow moves 10.

events.sizeChange: (size: number[]) while dragging and on every key
events.sizeChangeEnd: (size: number[]) when a drag or a key press ends

keyboard: Tab moves to each handle in turn
Arrow Left / Right (horizontal) or Up / Down (vertical) move the focused handle by keyboardStep percent; with Shift, 10. Right-to-left, Left and Right are mirrored (the engine's keys)
Home / End: the panel before the handle shrinks to its minimum / grows to its maximum
Enter collapses or expands a collapsible panel (the engine's key)
F6 moves to the next handle (the engine's key)
notes: Each handle is role=separator with aria-valuenow (the size of the panel before it), aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax, aria-orientation (perpendicular to the layout) and aria-controls naming both panels.
Name the handles with handleLabel ("Resize" by default); give the panels their own headings when they have names.
Resizing is never animated: the panels follow the pointer 1:1 and a key moves them at once.

motion: panels: no transition; they follow the pointer 1:1 while dragged and change at once from the keyboard
handle hover (a real pointer only): line → ink-3 over duration.fast; while dragged: accent at once; back to line over duration.fast
grip: never moves on its own

first paint: the panels are laid out at their given sizes from the first frame; a collapsible panel given its collapsed size is shut from the first frame (its minSize only applies once it is open; React renders a frame before the engine resolves the sizes, so its adapter holds the collapsed minimum meanwhile)
